Exact times in a time zone: Temporal's ZonedDateTime

Source: R/zoned-date-time.R
zoned_date_time.Rd

A zoned_date_time() is an exact time together with the time zone it is read in, so that it has both an instant() and a wall-clock date and time. Every element carries its own zone (design 4.2): the vector is an instant() with an integer zone code per element into the zones attribute, the identifiers in the database's case. The constructor is Temporal.ZonedDateTime and Temporal.ZonedDateTime.from() in one.

Usage

zoned_date_time(
  year,
  month = NULL,
  day = NULL,
  hour = 0,
  minute = 0,
  second = 0,
  millisecond = 0,
  microsecond = 0,
  nanosecond = 0,
  ...,
  time_zone = NULL,
  month_code = NULL,
  offset_string = NULL,
  disambiguation = "compatible",
  offset = "reject",
  overflow = "constrain"
)

zoned_date_time_compare(x, y)

Arguments

year

The year, or a string in RFC 9557 form with the zone in brackets ("2026-03-07T12:00[America/New_York]", "2026-03-07T12:00-05:00[America/New_York]", "2026-03-07T17:00Z[Europe/Lisbon]" for the instant shown in that zone, "2026-03-07[+05:30]" for the start of that day), or a zoned_date_time() to return as is.

month, day

The month (1 to 12) and day of the month, when year is a number. month may be replaced by month_code.

hour, minute, second, millisecond, microsecond, nanosecond

The time fields, 0 by default.

...

Must be empty.

time_zone

The time zone of each value, when year is a number: an IANA identifier such as "Europe/Lisbon", "UTC", or a fixed offset such as "+05:30"; recycled with the fields. Identifiers match regardless of case and are stored in the database's case.

month_code

The month as "M01" to "M12", instead of month.

offset_string

The UTC offset the fields are given in, such as "-05:00", when the fields carry one (Temporal's offset field); offset decides what happens when it disagrees with the zone.

disambiguation

How to resolve a local time in a clock gap or fold: "compatible", "earlier", "later" or "reject".

offset

What to do with a UTC offset that disagrees with the zone: "reject", "use", "ignore" or "prefer".

overflow

"constrain" (the default) clamps each field to its range, "reject" raises a zutempo_range_error (design 6.2).

x, y

zoned_date_time() values or strings, for zoned_date_time_compare(), which orders by the instant alone.

Value

A zoned_date_time() vector; zoned_date_time_compare() returns an integer vector of -1, 0 and 1.

Details

A local time that does not exist (a clock gap) or exists twice (a fold) is resolved by disambiguation (design 6.3): "compatible" (the default) moves a gap forward by its length and takes the earlier of a fold, "earlier" and "later" take that side, "reject" raises a zutempo_range_error. When the fields or the string carry a UTC offset as well as a zone, offset says what to do when the two disagree: "reject" (the default for the constructor) raises, "use" trusts the offset, "ignore" trusts the zone, "prefer" (the default for temporal_with()) trusts the offset when it is one of the zone's candidates and the zone otherwise.

Examples

zoned_date_time("2026-03-07T12:00[America/New_York]")
#> <zutempo_zoned_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-07T12:00:00-05:00[America/New_York]
zoned_date_time(2026, 3, 8, 2, 30, time_zone = "America/New_York")
#> <zutempo_zoned_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-03-08T03:30:00-04:00[America/New_York]
zoned_date_time(2026, 11, 1, 1, 30, time_zone = "America/New_York",
  disambiguation = "later")
#> <zutempo_zoned_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-11-01T01:30:00-05:00[America/New_York]
zoned_date_time("2026-07-01T12:00+05:30[Asia/Kolkata]")
#> <zutempo_zoned_date_time[1]>
#> [1] 2026-07-01T12:00:00+05:30[Asia/Kolkata]
zoned_date_time_compare(
  "2026-03-07T12:00[America/New_York]",
  "2026-03-07T18:00[Europe/Lisbon]"
)
#> [1] -1
